title: Astigmatism Before Surgery

patient.name: Mr Krishnan Murugan
patient.presenting_complaint: Listed for cataract surgery with significant astigmatism — topography requested for planning

history.hpc: Mr Krishnan says 'Doctor say my eye got a lot of astigmatism, need special lens for the operation.' He has a cataract with significant corneal astigmatism, and topography/keratometry is requested to plan a toric intraocular lens.
history.pmhx: Cataract with significant corneal astigmatism. No previous eye surgery. Dry eye.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Cataract; regular corneal astigmatism; reduced tear film

corneal_topography.purpose: Map the magnitude and axis of corneal astigmatism to plan a toric IOL
corneal_topography.result: Regular astigmatism with a defined steep axis recorded for the surgeon
corneal_topography.quality: Good capture after optimising the tear film; consistent on repeat

diagnosis: Corneal topography/keratometry maps the magnitude and axis of regular corneal astigmatism to plan a toric intraocular lens for cataract surgery. The tear film is optimised first (dry eye can distort readings), good-quality consistent maps are obtained, and the values are provided to the surgeon. The OT does not select the lens.

immediate: Confirm identity and the operative eye against the surgical listing
Optimise the ocular surface (stable tear film) before mapping, as dry eye distorts readings
Explain the non-contact scan and position the patient on the corneal apex
Capture good-quality maps and confirm the astigmatism magnitude and axis on repeat
Record the keratometry values and steep axis accurately
Provide the values to the surgeon for toric IOL planning
Document the findings and capture quality
follow_up: Surgeon to plan the toric IOL power and alignment axis
Re-map if readings are inconsistent due to dry eye
patient_education: Explain the scan measures the astigmatism to choose the right lens
Advise using lubricant drops to keep the surface healthy before surgery
Reassure it is quick and non-contact

key_points: Confirms identity and the correct operative eye
Notes the dry eye as relevant to accuracy
Explains the procedure and its purpose
Optimises the tear film before mapping
Records the astigmatism magnitude and steep axis accurately
Understands topography/keratometry guides toric IOL planning
Knows dry eye can distort the readings
Does not select the lens — provides values to the surgeon
Recognises the importance of an accurate axis
Provides accurate values to the surgeon
Advises on ocular surface care before surgery
